subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add diagnostics-only declared/effective tool visibility first, or also add a default-off strict inheritance mode that fails sessions when declared and effective tools diverge?
rationale: This changes the authority boundary between agent config and lower runtime/session security layers, and it adds config/protocol surface in an area where repository policy requires explicit security and product direction.

options.title: Diagnostics First
options.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, provider, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

options.title: Default-Off Strict Parity
options.body: Add a strict inheritance option that fails closed when declared and effective tools diverge, with explicit override-layer reporting and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Existing Clipping
options.body: Keep the current runtime-clipping model and document that declared agent tool config is not final session authority.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics First
recommendation.body: Expose declared, effective, and removed tools with structured reasons while keeping sandbox, subagent, ACP, provider, and runtime-host clipping authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the scoped capability profile, runtime tool policy, and gateway visibility surfaces where steipete has the clearest recent foundation work.
